summary: Renadyl is a three-strain probiotic (Streptococcus thermophilus, Lactobacillus acidophilus, Bifidobacterium longum) marketed for 'enteric dialysis', the idea that gut bacteria can metabolize urea and other nitrogenous waste. It is the only kidney-marketed supplement in this list with published trials of the product itself, all small and most sponsored or co-authored by its maker, Kibow Biotech.
evidence: Ranganathan 2009 (Canada): 6-month double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover pilot in 16 patients with CKD stages 3 to 4 (13 completed). BUN fell during probiotic periods versus placebo (mean change -2.93 vs +4.52 mmol/L, p = 0.002); creatinine did not change significantly. Sponsor-authored.

Ranganathan 2010 (four countries): 6-month crossover pilot in 46 patients with CKD stages 3 to 4 at 90 billion CFU/day. BUN fell in 63% of patients; creatinine and uric acid changes were not significant. Authors note small size and inconsistencies. Sponsor-authored.

Natarajan 2014 (hemodialysis): double-blind crossover RCT, 22 of 28 completed. No statistically significant change in uremic toxins or quality of life; trends only for white cell count, CRP and indoxyl glucuronide. Safe over 2-month periods.

Kalidindi 2024 (India): open-label RCT, 60 patients with CKD stages 3 to 4, Renadyl versus another probiotic (Lobun Forte) for 6 months, no placebo arm. Both arms reported lower indoxyl sulfate, BUN and creatinine. Co-authored by the comparator's manufacturer.

Class evidence: a meta-analysis of 14 RCTs found microbiota-directed therapy lowered p-cresyl sulfate but not indoxyl sulfate, and probiotics alone did not lower either (Chen 2022); a meta-analysis of 12 RCTs in non-dialysis patients found no effect of prebiotics, probiotics or synbiotics on serum creatinine (Liu 2023).
cautions: Probiotic organisms can enter the bloodstream: whole-genome sequencing has linked Lactobacillus bacteremia in ICU patients to the probiotic capsule they were given. Avoid in critically ill patients, those with a central venous catheter (including a tunneled hemodialysis catheter), recent bowel surgery or gut barrier injury, and in kidney transplant recipients or others on immunosuppression unless the treating team agrees. [Yelin 2019]
Trial outcomes were blood urea nitrogen (BUN), creatinine, uremic-toxin levels and quality-of-life scores; no trial reports kidney failure, dialysis start, cardiovascular events or death.

The published Renadyl trials used product from Kibow Biotech; the Philippine sheet names Wecare Probiotics (China) as manufacturer and gives no strain designations, so it cannot be confirmed that the strains and counts match the product that was studied.
Registered as a food supplement with no approved therapeutic claims: viable count, strain identity and storage stability are not verified by the FDA the way drug content is.
It does not replace evidence-based CKD care (blood pressure and glucose control, RAAS blockade, SGLT2 inhibitors where indicated, diet).
bottom_line: Small, mostly sponsor-linked trials show changes in BUN or uremic toxins at best, with no evidence on kidney or patient outcomes. Reasonable to tolerate in a stable outpatient who wants it; avoid in transplant recipients, the immunosuppressed, the critically ill and patients with a dialysis catheter; never a substitute for proven CKD therapy.

guideline_heading: What the Philippine product sheet states
guideline: Distributor: Goodfellow Pharma Corporation (Pasig City). Manufacturer: Wecare Probiotics Co., Ltd. (Suzhou, Jiangsu, China).

Each capsule: Bifidobacterium longum, Streptococcus thermophilus and Lactobacillus acidophilus, 15 billion CFU each (45 billion CFU per capsule); no strain designations are given. 60 capsules per box, in blisters.
Directions on the sheet: 1 to 2 capsules twice daily with or right after a meal, for a full 3 months, or as advised by a health professional.
Side effects named on the sheet: mild gas or flatulence that usually settles within 2 to 3 weeks. Storage: cool, dry place at 15 to 25 °C, protected from light.
The sheet's mechanism (microbes in the colon consuming nitrogenous wastes that diffuse from the blood) is the maker's description; the FDA registration carries no approved therapeutic claims.
